claims.text: The same release records that he took part in the second French Antarctic expedition in 1958, building the Dumont d'Urville base in Adélie Land, was an alumnus of the École Normale Supérieure (Ulm), agrégé de sciences physiques and docteur ès sciences, held the chair of Space Techniques and Programmes at the CNAM for many years, and died aged 80 on 26 February 2013.

CNES's own press release on Lebeau's death gives his career: he founded and directed the Groupe de recherches ionosphériques from 1961, became 'Directeur des programmes et du plan du CNES' in 1965 and then 'Directeur général adjoint, chargé des programmes et de la politique industrielle', joined ESA in 1975 rising to Deputy Director General, was Directeur de la Météorologie Nationale and then Directeur général de Météo France, President of Eumetsat from 1990, Vice-President of the World Meteorological Organization 1991-1994, and 'président du CNES (1995-1996)'.

title: CNES, communiqué de presse CP009-2013, 'Le CNES rend hommage à André Lebeau', 28 février 2013
